Library functions will produce ConfigUpdate envelopes ready for signing but will not execute the signature workflow themselves (except in examples).
assumptions: The developer is already familiar with Hyperledger Fabric configuration internals and Go tooling, so no training time is included.
The existing Fabric build and test infrastructure is available and the code will be added to the Fabric source tree or a compatible fork.
The function config.UpdateOrdererConfiguration either already exists or requires only trivial adaptation; this increment focuses on the retrieval helper.
Certificate inputs are PEM-encoded; revocation uses DER/PEM CRL as per Fabric MSP.
Unit tests beyond the mentioned example tests are required as part of professional development, though not explicitly requested.
Effort estimates exclude code review cycles, CI waiting time, and elapsed calendar duration; they represent pure development workdays.
All required config block/transaction parsing utilities are available in the current Fabric version (release-1.4 era as per spec links).
